extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and immunology/vaccine researchers conducting preclinical and translational Staphylococcus aureus vaccine studies
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and executing a translational research program to identify protective versus non-protective human anti-S. aureus antibodies and to test vaccine candidates in naïve and SA-exposed hosts (preclinical and human-serology driven studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: We anticipate 100 subjects (75 children and 25 older adults) enrolled over the first four years ... This sample size will provide sufficient power (80%) to detect at least a 1.9-fold increase in the odds of protection per standard-deviation titer increase for each antigen, with a significance level to 0.001 corresponding to a conservative Bonferonni-type correction for 65 antigens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes expected distribution of sera categories (50% non-protective, 40% moderately protective, 10% highly protective) and links power to logistic regression analyses; conservative multiple-comparison correction applied (α≈0.001) for 65 antigens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and sex as biological variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Children and older adults of both sexes will be recruited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit monitoring of age/sex source in in vitro experiments; in vivo experiments performed with male and female mice; design considers pediatric vs older adult comparisons and explores mechanistic differences related to aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative/repository samples if enrollment wanes
rubrics_metrics.description: If collection of clinical isolates, sera, and cells declines, we will draw on our previously collected repository containing >250 invasive samples, consented for future use of leftover samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository can supplement with a small number of subjects but lacks sufficient serum volume to fully support the proposal — used as contingency rather than primary data source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquid bead array assay QC and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a liquid bead array to test the Ab-antigen interaction of patient sera is attractive due to its efficiency and reproducibility. However, these arrays can be difficult to use correctly while maintaining the integrity of the proteins in question (e.g., improper conjugation of an antigen to the array would result in a false negative result).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maximize rigor, extensive controls will be used in addition to technical reproducibility and validation by ELISA. Anti-human IgG will be used to confirm the addition of sample and negative controls including buffer and antigen tag controls will also be used to ensure the antigen is properly bound to the array.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preselected antigen panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess specific Ab against 10 SA antigens of particular interest ... Cell-surface antigens (IsdA, MntC*, ClfA*, SpA, FhuD2, EsxAB), PAMPs (LTA*, Lipoprotein*) and toxins (Hla*, LukED) with * denoting vaccine trials that demonstrated lack of efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel includes known virulence determinants and antigens that failed clinical trials; used in parallel with candidate protective antigens from Aim 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of candidate protective antigens (ranking criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank list will be based on relative titer of specific Ab in protective samples vs. non-protective samples ... determine which SA antigens are independently predictive of functional protection in human pediatric sera following invasive infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antigens selected from logistic regression analyses (continuous Ab levels) and top-ranked antigens (8 highest-ranked) are advanced to study; provision of 8 alternative antigens if fewer than 8 non-overlapping candidates are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purification and functional evaluation of antigen-specific antibodies
rubrics_metrics.description: We will purify specific Ab using antigen columns, then evaluate the Ab for protection in the transfer model. Protection will be evaluated by determination of the protection upon specific depletion of the Ab from that sample, where loss of protection signifies function of the depleted Abs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affinity columns generated with antigens; eluate used to generate specific-Ab depleted sera (see Fig.12B). Depletion approach preserves interaction between Ab and other serum factors; loss-of-function upon depletion used as evidence of Ab protective role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and sampling strategy for protective vs non-protective sera
rubrics_metrics.description: For each antigen target, we will aim to test protective sera from 5 pediatric and 5 older adult individuals at the peak of protection (usually 6 weeks) and after the protection has subsided (at 6 months). When available, we would like to similarly test the sera from up to 5 individuals with moderate to high titer but not protective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparing protective and non-protective sera (and individuals with high titers but no protection) to reveal antibody features important for conferring protection; sample selection favors extremes of protection within antibody groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strain selection and antigen expression confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The study will utilize primarily LAC, a prototype USA300 epidemic strain ... we will corroborate RNA expression of the specific SA antigen by USA300 in vivo prior to proceeding with each study. A collection of other SA strains is available if USA300 does not express the antigen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reduced Ab efficacy might derive from non-conserved sequences, evaluate function in vitro using LAC and the infecting SA isolate obtained from that subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recombinant antigen production QC
rubrics_metrics.description: Recombinant SA antigens expressed from E. coli will be LPS detoxified using a spun-column and purified on an affinity (nickel), then seizing column. Additional QC include appropriate functional assays on each prep to verify and quantify protein function, e.g. cytolysis per µg of toxins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional assays required for each prep to ensure antigen integrity and activity prior to affinity column generation for antibody purification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoptive transfer in vivo protection assay parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: We will inject C57BL/6 mice (n=8) IV with the equivalent of 100 µl of purified human specific Ab IV. After 6h, we will challenge the mice with 10^7 late log-phase SA (USA300 strain LAC) IV and measure spleen and kidney CFUs and IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6 and tissue histopathology at 48h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoptive transfer is primary readout for protection; group size n=8; endpoints at 48h; used to define protection and to corroborate in vitro findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro functional assay selection by antigen class
rubrics_metrics.description: For cell surface adhesins, we will perform opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays using standard methods. For toxins, cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion in toxin-tropic human and mouse cell lines will be used. For secreted enzymes, we will use assays tailored to test the enzymatic function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPK: SA preincubated with sera for 15 mins added to THP1 or mouse bone-marrow derived neutrophils at MOI 10:1 for 1 hour and CFU enumerated. Toxin neutralization: recombinant toxin incubated with control or test sera prior to addition to appropriate host cells; measure cytolysis and cytokines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and hierarchy of evidence for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection will be primarily evaluated based on the in vivo adoptive transfer assay. In case of marginally significant protection, evidence from the in vitro assays will be used as secondary supportive evidence. Criteria for in vivo protection are ... based on CFU and histopathology at 48h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reliance on in vivo assay; in vitro assays provide secondary support for marginal results; explicit quantitative endpoints (CFU, histopathology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of antibodies and subject samples for structural/functional profiling
rubrics_metrics.description: From the list of antigens evaluated in Aim 2.1., we will investigate up to 10 anti-SA Ab, ideally 4 against 'protective' antigens, and 6 against 'non-protective' antigens. We will aim to include toxins, cell-wall anchored adhesins and secreted proteins. We will aim to study serum samples from up to 10 individuals, preferentially picking individual samples that provide highest or lowest levels of protection within the specific antibody group (after controlling for titers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection maximizes contrasts (protective vs non-protective; high vs low protection) and explores age-related differences if identified in Aim2.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody profiling assay battery
rubrics_metrics.description: We will perform 3 types of assays that will inform on antibody protective functions: I. Titer and Ig class / subclass. II. Fab-mediated antigen neutralization: (1) Ag binding avidity using a urea stringency assay, (2) Epitope mapping by BCR sequencing, B cell hybridoma generation and mapping using overlapping peptides, (3) Neutralization/functional assays. III. Protection related to Fc interaction with complement and phagocytes: (1) glycan analysis, (2) complement binding assay, (3) OPK by human neutrophils, (4) Ab mediated neutrophil phagocytosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equimolar antibody quantities for functional comparisons; map epitopes for selected antigens (IsdB, IsdA, Hla) and correlate epitope with neutralization; corroborate suggested functions using genetic or pharmacologic inhibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on resource-intensive assays (epitope mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because mapping of epitope is effort and resource intensive, we will limit to 3 Ab targeting SA antigens, IsdB (not yet performed on human Ab), IsdA and Hla, which have well-defined protective subdomain(s). For each antigen, we will seek out the 2 most and 2 least neutralizing Ab from the samples and correlate the epitope map ... to their neutralizing activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize mapping where structural data exist; focus on extremes of neutralization to maximize informative contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing short duration of protective memory
rubrics_metrics.description: For up to 3 of the protective antigens that exhibit loss of Ab protection at 6 months, we will compare the structural and functional profile of the same antibodies at 6 weeks and 6 months after SA infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If titer differences suspected, assess equimolar concentrations across timepoints; findings used to inform strategies to overcome short-lived memory (e.g., adjuvants).

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro reproducibility standards
rubrics_metrics.description: In vitro experiments throughout the project will be done in triplicate and repeated at least three times to assure reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primary cells or cell lines from mice or human of both sexes; note age/gender source of cells in case differences emerge; tri-replicate and independent repeats required.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo reproducibility and group sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: All in vivo experiments will be done with groups of at least 8 age- and sex- matched animals as we have determined that this group size is sufficient to detect the differences being tested using α=0.05 and power=0.8. Experiments will be performed at least twice (n = 4 x 2 exps) to assure reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum n=8 per group, both sexes, matched by age/sex; experiments repeated independently to confirm findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for selecting vaccine antigens for active immunization studies
rubrics_metrics.description: We will select 8 SA antigens from Aim 2.1/2.2 ... For the protective antigens, we will determine if the vaccines are protective in both naïve and SA-experienced hosts. For non-protective antigens, we will preferentially pick antigens that failed clinical trials ... All antigens should 1) induce protection in naïve mice as a vaccine (this is already confirmed for to the 18 SA antigens listed in Aim 2), and 2) should induce at least moderate level of Ab response to SA to permit the effect of prior specific humoral immunity on vaccination to be studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to include a mix (1/3 to 1/2) of protective antigens; if antigen not protective in naïve mice, replace with alternative meeting criteria; multiple antigen types (toxins, adhesins, secreted factors) prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active vaccination and challenge protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: To simulate exposure to SA, we will inoculate mice with 10^7 SA (LAC) or PBS control IP at weekly intervals x 2-3, ... Ten days after, we will immunize the mice with 2.5 µg of LPS-depleted, column-purified antigen in alum at weekly intervals x 3, then challenge the mice 10 days after with the same SA strain. We will measure CFU and tissue IL1β, IL6, IL17A, IFNγ, IL23, IL10, TGFβ and histopathology from spleen and kidneys at 48h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adoptive transfer of serum to corroborate Ab-mediated protection; use humanized mice where human tropism suspected; validate specificity using isogenic deletion mutants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passive immunization evaluation schedule and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: We will assess the efficacy of 4 anti-SA human monoclonal Ab in mice that have been pre-injected with human sera. Each mAb will be matched with human samples with either high or low levels of specific Ab against the corresponding antigen (5 high and 5 low). We will inject mice IV with 100 µL of human sera, followed 4h later with SA challenge, then 6h later with the mAb (dosed to simulate the clinical trial). Controls will consist of mAb alone, isotype control and the human serum alone. Readouts at 24h post infection will consist of tissue CFU, cytokines and histopathology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To verify that any interference is antigen specific, deplete the antigen-specific Ab by passage through an affinity column and determine whether interference is abrogated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic interrogation of vaccine interference
rubrics_metrics.description: We will evaluate immune imprinting and Ab competition mechanisms: purify SA antigen-specific B cells and analyze B-cell receptors for memory clonal expansion; measure antigen-specific IgM at 3 and 7 days after vaccination to look for prompt recall activation; assay antibodies from different settings for titers, affinity, glycan profile, OPK, complement binding, cytolysis and epitope mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If analyses point to specific reasons for loss of Ab function (e.g., glycosylation differences linked to IL10), perform inhibition experiments (anti-IL10, FcR mutants, glycan removal) to corroborate causal mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting subdominant antigens strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify SA antigens that induced low or no Ab in our pediatric study ... investigate 3 antigens (including SdrE) in passive and active vaccination studies. Active vaccines: corroborate efficacy in naïve mice. Passive vaccines: assess if the subdominant vaccine is more effective by performing passive transfer of the protective antibodies into mice pre-injected with human sera with low corresponding SA antigen-specific Ab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: subdominant antigens may avoid recall of interfering non-protective Ab; evaluate multiple subdominant antigens because human vaccine is likely multi-target; verify Ab-mediated protection via adoptive transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan and decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-group analysis will use either unpaired two-tailed t-test or a non-parametric Mann–Whitney U-test in the case of missing normality. Comparisons of multiple groups will be performed using one-way ANOVA and subsequent Bonferroni multiple comparisons. If normality or equal variance tests fail, then a Kruskal-Wallis test and subsequent Dunn’s multiple comparisons will be used. Correlation analyses will be performed using linear regression and evaluation of R2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply normality and equal-variance checks prior to test selection; control for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subject eligibility and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Children (age 6 months to 18 years) or adults (>65 years of age) admitted to Vanderbilt University Medical Center with culture-proven Staphylococcus aureus infection. Have provided informed consent and informed assent (when applicable) to participate in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children under 6 months excluded due to maternal IgG impact; informed assent for capable children; additional protections addressed under 45 CFR Part 46 Subpart D; enrollment and recruitment plans documented (recruitment and retention plan, timeline).
